site.name: Alie Belle Mine
site.location: Chalk Creek district, south of Romley
site.componentDetail: Underground gold-silver-lead-zinc mine with two documented adits
overview: The Alie Belle Mine—also documented as the Allie Belle—lies in the Chalk Creek mining district about one mile south of the former settlement of Romley. U.S. Geological Survey work describes two adits east of the historic Romley–Hancock road.

Federal mineral records identify the property as an underground past producer with gold as its principal commodity. Geological reporting also records lead, zinc, copper and silver-bearing sulfide minerals at the mine.

timeline.text: USGS Professional Paper 289 documented the mine's location, two-adit layout and mineral assemblage in its study of the Garfield quadrangle.

moreHistory: USGS mapping describes a lower adit near the mine locality and an upper adit about 350 feet to the southeast, providing a useful picture of the documented workings.
Reported minerals include pyrite, chalcopyrite, galena and sphalerite in quartz with sericite or muscovite.

The mapped point near 38.64952, -106.36739 represents the historical mine locality and lower-adit vicinity, not a field-surveyed confirmation of a currently open or accessible portal. Old mine workings are hazardous and access conditions may have changed.
